title: fix(gateway): make crashes visible after automatic restarts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes silent Gateway crashes: after an automatic restart, operators currently see a healthy fresh process with no product-visible record of the unexpected exit.

## User Impact

The next startup records and warns about the previous unexpected exit. The last ten crashes appear in Gateway status, Doctor findings, health RPC, and authorized readiness details. Clean shutdowns and planned restart handoffs do not create crash records. Windows task supervision and the macOS app retry unexpected child exits through bounded recovery, including signal deaths. The existing Control UI Debug health/status view receives these facts; there is no new UI chrome.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `gateway_boot_lifecycle` table remains the single clean/unclean receipt owner. Its startup worker transaction stores metadata and bounded history in the existing `config_machine_state` key `gateway.crashes`. There is no schema change, new config, heartbeat timer, or agent/workspace scan.

Rebased onto `b55baff690681d2d115e73d8b7ae996ff9f3274c`, including #194527, #194481 and #194509. Crash recording consumes the boot owner's newly computed predecessor window. The retained per-agent intervals in `gateway.restartRecovery` remain recovery work; an old pending interval cannot manufacture another crash after a clean boot. Startup failures are recorded without creating a resumable interval. Reporting and enrichment now form one lifecycle-owned operation; the separate reporting module and exported enrichment wrapper are removed.

Production delta is **+483 net LOC** (+573/-90; tests, tooling and docs excluded). This compression removes nine production lines from the first rebased candidate. The final delta is three lines above the previous pushed revision after restoring the optional status type contract and integrating the retained-window owner. Status, Doctor and startup warnings share `formatGatewayCrash`; health transports the structured record. The startup `try/finally` remains the existing settlement boundary. Remaining growth implements persistent bounded history, native evidence, operator surfaces and two supervisor recovery gaps; removing those would remove requested behavior.

The record path adds **no synchronous I/O or SQLite writes to request/turn hot paths**. Startup and post-startup enrichment use the existing boot worker. Safe-mode startup recovery retargets metadata inside its existing transaction. Existing clean-close and lease-heartbeat writes are unchanged; the previous heartbeat comes from the existing lock-acquisition read. Health/status/readiness use the bounded committed in-memory projection; CLI status and Doctor use asynchronous exact-key worker reads.

Systemd enrichment uses indexed `(MESSAGE_ID=98e322203f7a4ed290d09fe03c09fe15 AND UNIT=<unit>) OR (MESSAGE_ID=... AND USER_UNIT=<unit>)`, without grep. The exact stall marker is searched by PID and system/user unit in at most the final 30 seconds, ending at exit or detection and narrowed by heartbeat. Both queries share a monotonic one-second budget. At most ten newest exit rows are inspected; main-process discrimination prevents an `ExecStopPost` failure from replacing the Gateway cause. Only structured exit fields supply that cause. Missing evidence stays unknown; a failed marker lookup cannot erase known exit evidence.

## Evidence

- Final focused rebase proof: 143 tests passed, one Windows-only skip on macOS, covering lifecycle, retained restart intervals, native cause lookup, status and readiness. This includes all 29 lifecycle tests. The retained-window regression verifies a clean later boot creates neither another crash nor a duplicate history entry.
- The previously failing services and commands test typecheck leaves pass, along with core typechecking. The producer now explicitly owns optional crash details; mock journal-call indexing is checked. These repair the exact `check-test-types-core-3/core-4` failures on the prior head.
- Test-lines allocation is exactly **426 added LF**, with no inherited-debt allowance. Main #194509 reconciles its own prior debt. Total and ceiling both equal 6,561,226, with zero slack; this PR leaves the shared scalar unchanged.
- Fresh Codex autoreview of the complete final candidate against `b55baff690681d2d115e73d8b7ae996ff9f3274c` is **scoped-clean through P2**.


Fresh isolated `pnpm openclaw gateway run` proof passed on the reviewed source: SIGKILL → exactly one durable crash and one WARN; SIGTERM → another startup with neither; SIGUSR2 handoff → `planned_restart`, a successor receipt, and no additional crash or warning. Final outcomes were open crashed receipt / clean stop / planned restart / clean stop. All fixture Gateway PIDs exited. Foreground cause correctly remained unknown.

`pnpm check:changed` completed on the first rebase. Core and all core-test typecheck shards, scripts types, format, TypeScript/Swift lint, SQLite ownership/dialect checks, import-cycle and other guards passed. It was not wholly green: the archived-changelog gate reproduces the same 20 violations on exact parent `87c57b41c590` (current signature introduced by #194364 / `266a7aa0fe69`; its predecessor already had a different red signature). The production export scan also reproduced two parent findings, subsequently fixed by #194509 and included in the final rebase.

The broader macOS check failed `src/skills/runtime/discovery.integration.test.ts`, “discovers external edits without waiting for a periodic scan and shares one worker”: observed `Original` instead of `Final` after 15s. This remains an unresolved filesystem-watcher failure, not a claimed inherited-failure waiver. Later macOS command groups were not reached. The production-only export scan passes with zero findings after the final rebase.

Earlier exact-parent owner reproduction fails with zero crash facts and passes with one on the feature. The indexed-query regression fails on the earlier whole-run-grep implementation. The macOS supervisor's real SIGILL child proof fails before the retry fix and passes afterward. Native systemd/Windows execution is covered by contract fixtures rather than live services; the full macOS app suite remains CI coverage. No production host or data was accessed. No changed module is imported by `ui/src`; no new Node-only UI import was introduced. Main's prior UI-e2e regression is fixed by #194504.

Earlier synthetic measurement, before this rebase, used exact parent `1f7035c15f3d6f89b7336c0d273ddcb18b8ff060`, a 35 GiB agent database, 4,096 sessions and 62,000 workspace files. Owner SQL was 4 → 6, observed agent/workspace accesses zero, and history bounded at ten. Median wall 2.335 → 4.352 ms, CPU 1.886 → 2.296 ms, sampled allocation 113,392 → 142,179 bytes. A/A drift was 38.3% wall, 23.3% CPU and 1.2% allocation on the busy host, so no timing improvement is claimed. APFS and synthetic BLOB padding model volume, not btrfs or the full transcript distribution. These are retained historical measurements; #194527 adds shared recovery work, and absolute timings were not reprofiled for this rebase.

Final head: `84e08739e965e7d18b4d63fab785a5bc966a78ad`; committed patch bytes match the reviewed candidate.
